def: The research area of automatically creating agent designs, including new building blocks and new ways of combining them, instead of designing them by hand.
An ADAS algorithm in which a language model repeatedly writes new agents as code, tests them and stores them in an archive that informs the next proposal.
The language model, prompted to design other agents, that proposes each new candidate in a search over agent designs.
The set of agents a method can represent at all, which limits the best possible result before any search begins.
The scoring rule applied to each candidate agent, such as accuracy on a search set, which the search can only be as good as.
A growing store of every discovered agent with its score, kept even when an agent scored worse than its parent so that its ideas can be reused later.
The single function a meta agent writes to define an agent in the ADAS framework: it takes the task information and returns the agent's answer.
The upward bias in the score of the best of many noisy measurements, which grows with the number of candidates and shrinks with the size of the evaluation set.
Jeff Clune's programme of meta-learning architectures, learning algorithms and learning environments so that AI is produced by algorithms rather than hand design.
A solution or idea that does not score best when found but that later designs build on, which is why archives keep it.
